The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.80,00,000/ for the death of one Mahesh K.C. in a road traffic accident dated 08.11.2020.
2.
The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, That, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and the petitioner No.3 is the Mother of deceased.
On 08.11.2020 at about 05.15pm., the deceased was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA53U9934 on the left side of MD Pura ring Road service road from KR Pura Railway Station towards Marathahalli.

When the deceased reached infront of True Value Car Showroom, Bangalore city , a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA53B5539 driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life suddenly came in the same direction behind the motorcycle and hit the motorcycle.
Due to impact the deceased fell down and stuck to the left side front wheel and the Lorry dragged him about 10 feet and he died on the spot.
After conducting the PM, the body was handed over to the family of the deceased.
The petitioners have further claimed that they have spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards transportation and funeral obsequies.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 46 years, earning Rs.50,000/ per month from his Business.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the Lorry Driver and the KR Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against him in Cr.No.207/2020 p/u/Secs.279 & 304(A) of IPC.

The 1 st respondent being the RC owner, 2nd respondent being the insurance holder and the 3rd respondent being the insurer of the said offending Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Hence,

sentences.text: 3. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondent No.3 appeared and filed written statements.

In spite of due service of summons respondent Nos.1 & 2 did not appear and hence,
placed exparte.
4.

The objections of the Respondent No.3:
This respondent admits the issuance of policy in respect of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA53B5539 but denied the entire petition averments.
The driver of the vehicle did not have valid and effective DL as on the time of the accident and the Lorry did not have valid permit and FC.
They have stated that the Lorry was not involved in the accident.
They have also stated that the petition is not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.134(C) & 158(6) of MV Act.

Further denied the age,
income and avocation of the deceased and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Mahesh K.C.?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Mahesh K.C. died on account of road traffic accident took place on 08.11.2020 at about 5.15pm near MD Pura Ring road, Service road from KR Pura Railway Station towards Marathahalli, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA53U9934?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4.
What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined Two witnesses as PWs.1 & 2 and got marked 21 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 21.
On the other side the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any document.

7. Heard both Counsels and perused the materials on record.
The counsel for the petitioner has produced written arguments.
8.

My finding to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1 : In the affirmative Issue Nos.2 & 3: In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:

3 9.
Issue No.1:
In order to prove that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and has reiterated about the relationship in her affidavit in chief.
In addition she got marked DL of the deceased, Ration Card of the family, the Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the school admission certificate of the deceased as per Exs.P.16 to P.19.
According to Ex.P.16, the name of the father of the deceased was Chinnappaji.
According to Ex.P.17 petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
The Aadhar cards of the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 also show the husband's and father's name as Mahesh K.C.
The Aadhar card of the petitioner No.3 shows her husband's name as Chinnappa.
Moreover as per Ex.P.19 school Admission certificate of the deceased mother's name is shown as Puttamma i.e., the petitioner No.3.
Therefore, the Tribunal holds that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
10. Issue No.2:

The Petitioners, to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry have examined First Petitioner/Wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 8.
They also got examined an eye witness to the accident as PW.2.
During the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
During the cross examination of PW.2 he has stated that the service road was a Two way road.
He has also stated that the bike did not get damaged to the back portion except to the right side crash guard & to the front portion.
He has admitted that in case of damage to the right side crash guard, the rider should have fallen to the left side.
11. The FIR was registered on the same day as per Ex.P.1 and the charge sheet is also filed by the police as per Ex.P.3.
As per the sketch at Ex.P.4 the Lorry has hit the Two wheeler from behind and both the vehicles were traveling towards the same direction.
According to Ex.P.6, the damages to the Lorry is to the left front portion, whereas the motorcycle has suffered damages to the front head light assembly, front left handle and left hand crash guard.
The respondent No.3 has contended that there was non involvement of the Lorry in the accident.
But in order to prove the same they have neither produced any document nor examined any witness.
From the IMV report it is clear that the Lorry has hit the right crash guard of the bike and the deceased has fallen to the right side and thereby coming under the left wheel of the Lorry.

Therefore, on the basis of the documents before the court it is clear that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the Lorry driver and the petitioner died as per the report at Exs.P.7 & 8 i.e., PM report and Inquest Mahazar.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No. 3:
The petitioners have proved that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the mother of the deceased.
There is nothing elicited by the respondent No.3 during the cross examination of PW.1 to show that they were not dependents of the deceased.
Therefore, all three are held to be dependents of the deceased.

To show the deceased's income they have produced Exs.P.9 to 15 and P.20 & P.21 i.e., copy of VAT Registration certificate alongwith annexure, acknowledgment of payment of PT and enrollment certificate for the year 2014,
entrepreneurs Memorandum Part I Acknowledgment, Entrepreneur Memorandum Part II Acknowledgment, Two IT returns for the year 201415 and 201516 alongwith statement of income,
National Trade Certificate, National Apprenticeship certificate, service certificate of deceased dated Veena R.K vs S.Kodandarama on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116065558/
4 18.12.1998 and Employment and Training marks sheet.
Exs.P.9 to 12 show that the deceased was carrying on the business under the name of 'AVM Industries' from 2008.
The IT returns produced at Ex.P.13 relate to the year 201415 and 201516.
Exs. P.14
are certificates about the skills of the deceased.
However, the petitioners have not filed any Bank Statement or Auditor's report to show the monthly income of the deceased from his business.
Hence the court has to take notional income.

13. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.7404/2014 (MVD), by referring on the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Meena Pawaria and others Vs. Ashrafali and others (2021 SCC online sc 1083), Jakir Hussein Vs. Sabir (2015) 7 SCC 252, Smt. Neeta and others Vs. Divisional Manager, MSRTC Kolhapur (2015)3 scc 590, Kala Devi and Orthers Vs. Bhagwan Das Chouhan and Others (2015) 2 SCC 771, Sonobanu Nazirbhai Mirza Vs. Ahmadabad Municipal Transport Service (2013) 16 SCC 719, Pushkar Mehra Vs. Brij Mohan Kushwaha and others (2015)
12 SCC 688, Govind Yadav Vs. The New India Insurance Company Limited and another (2011) 10 SCC 683 and Ningamma and another Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited (2009) 13 SCC 710 has held that there is a continuous and consistent trend by the Apex Court that the Minimum Wages Act provide for a source by which the notional income of the deceased, who had no valid proof of income could be assessed. .......The range of the wages between highly skilled and unskilled labour may have to be considered by the Tribunal while assessing the income of the deceased........

sentences.text: However, such guidelines cannot take the place of statutory guidelines and therefore we hold that it would be proper to rely on the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act as a guideline and assess whether the deceased was a skilled or unskilled laborer.

14. It is pertinent to note that as per the Karnataka Government Notification of Minimum Wages from 01.04.2020 to 31.03.2021 for employment in Turner, Turner Die.Polisher, Operator, Welder,
Welder, Melter, Moulder etc., the monthly income is Rs.15,316/ per month.
Therefore the notional income of the deceased can be rounded off to Rs.15,500/ per month.
Age of the deceased 15.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of DL of the deceased as per Ex.P.16.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
As per said document, the date of birth of the deceased was 15.07.1974 and the accident occurred on 08.11.2020.
As such, the age of the deceased is 46 years as on the date of accident.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased comes 4050 years age slab, 25% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
Therefore, Rs.3,875/ future prospectus is to be added to his monthly income, then it comes to Rs.19,375/.
As per Principles laid down in the case of Sarala Verma the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 13.
The deceased has a wife, a daughter and a mother.

Veena R.K vs S.Kodandarama on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116065558/
5
They are all dependents of the deceased.

Since there are Three dependents then 1/3 of the income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.12,917/
(Rs.19,375/  Rs.6,458/).

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.20,15,052/
(Rs.12,917/ X 13 x 12 = Rs.20,15,052/).
ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018)
18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to her family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

16. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
17.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 43 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/ under the head of loss of consortium.
Similarly, the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 are the daughter and mother of the deceased, they have lost their loving, care taking father and Son.
Therefore, they are also entitled to Rs.44,000/ each, in total Rs.1,32,000/ is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.
iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.
As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.21,87,052/.

If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.21,87,100/.
LIABILITY 18.
The respondents have failed to prove their defence by leading evidence.

Therefore, the respondents No.1 to 3 being the owner, insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the Petitioners and satisfy the award.
Though the Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.80,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,82,600/ with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.

6
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.4:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for  Compensation of Rs.21,87,100/ (Rupees Twenty One lakhs Eigty Seven Thousand One Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However,
the Respondent No.3 being the insurer is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.
On deposit of the award amount and interest, 25% each shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 in any N/S bank for a period of 3 years.

Out of the total compensation Rs.2,00,000/ each shall be released to the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 and remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of epayment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
